prerequisites: Basic knowledge for explaining and interpreting various concepts and processes associated with the fundamental field of engineering sciences.

learning_outcomes.text: Explains the fundamentals of exergy, exergoeconomics, and exergoecology.
Describes the concepts of irreversibility, exergy destruction, and exergetic efficiencies.
Knows the structure of exergoeconomic analysis methods (SPECO, CGAM, TBM methods, etc.).
Understands the relationships between energy, exergy, economic, and environmental analysis.
Identifies the mechanisms of exergetic losses in real mechanical and thermal systems.
Knows the economic models applied to processes in mechanical engineering.
Applies exergetic models for the analysis of components (turbines, compressors, heat exchangers, pumps, thermal engines).
Uses exergoeconomic methods to calculate costs associated with exergy flows.
Develops exergetic and exergoeconomic balances for complex systems.
Analyzes the influence of operating parameters on exergetic and economic performance.
Uses software tools for numerical exergetic analyses.
Formulates engineering recommendations for the energetic and economic optimization of systems.
Assumes responsibility for the correct execution of exergetic and exergoeconomic models.
Demonstrates autonomy in scientific documentation and the use of modern analysis methods.
Integrates energetic, economic, and sustainability criteria in system evaluation.
Develops own professional competences, adopting efficient and ethical practices.
Integrates into multidisciplinary technical teams, contributing with well-founded complex analyses.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to exergy, exergoeconomics, and exergoecology. Differences from energy analysis
Fundamentals of exergy: physical, chemical, mechanical exergy. Exergy balances
Irreversibilities and exergy destruction. Sources of losses in mechanical systems
Exergoeconomic analysis: methods for calculating exergetic costs (SPECO, CGAM, FW)
Exergoecological analysis: environmental costs, impact of destroyed exergy, pollution
Applications in mechanical engineering: turbines, compressors, engines, heat pumps, industrial installations
Exergetic and exergoeconomic optimization of systems. Multi-criteria analysis
Determination of exergetic efficiencies for mechanical components
Exergoeconomic model for a simple system (turbine, compressor)
Exergoecological analysis: environmental costs, impact factors
Exergoeconomic optimization. Practical examples and interpretation
teaching_methods: Case studies from mechanical and energy industry
Recapitulation of essential concepts and gradual introduction of advanced notions
Graphical and economic interpretation of exergetic balances

assessment_methods.method: Exam (comprising formative evaluation test and summative evaluation test)
Seminar (comprising active participation and evaluation test)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of minimal learning outcomes. A minimum grade of 5 is required for both the Exam and Seminar components. The Exam component itself is composed of a formative evaluation test (20%) and a summative evaluation test (80%).
